reason: The bone-lineage environment is the visible cue for directing stem-cell descendants toward bone-forming cells.
expectation: The signals should produce a bone-lineage cell population.

effect: The signals produced bone cells, including matrix-producing osteoblasts and embedded osteocytes; I can now assemble the bone components.
reaction: The distinction between the two bone-cell roles is useful.
reason: Calcium phosphate mineral belongs in the collagen framework of the same bones, so combining them should build their supporting material.
expectation: The mineral will reinforce the collagen framework to form mineralized bone matrix.

effect: The collagen framework is now mineralised, showing how collagen and mineral contribute different mechanical properties.
reaction: The contrast between toughness and compression resistance is useful.
reason: Bone cells belong in the mineralised framework and are needed to build living bone.
expectation: The cells will be incorporated into the arm bone framework.

effect: The mineralised framework now contains bone cells, but its blood supply is still missing.
reaction: The fine channels make the embedded cells easier to picture.
reason: The unfilled vessel outline and the goal of supplied bones point directly to adding blood vessels.
expectation: The vessels will supply the living arm bones.

effect: The vessels completed the living arm bones, revealing a goal to connect them into a supported, movable joint.
reaction: The cutaway usefully separates the vessel, cells and matrix.
reason: The synovial membrane is described as lining the inner face of a joint sleeve, matching the capsule goal.
expectation: The membrane will line the sleeve to form a joint capsule.

effect: The synovial membrane lined the fibrous sleeve, completing the capsule; the bones still need to be connected into a supported, movable joint.
reaction: The distinction between the lining and the outer sleeve is clear.
reason: Articular cartilage forms smooth caps on the bone ends, so adding it to the living bones is a logical step toward the joint.
expectation: The cartilage will cover the bones' joint surfaces.

effect: The arm bones now have smooth cartilage caps on their facing elbow surfaces.
reaction: The sliding inset makes the cartilage's role clear.
reason: The synovial capsule surrounds the joint cavity, so combining it with the capped bones should assemble the elbow.
expectation: The capsule will surround the cartilage-covered bone ends.

effect: The capsule now encloses the cartilage-covered bone ends, with fluid in the joint space; the joint still needs support.
reaction: The description connects the lining's fluid to gliding surfaces.
reason: The elbow ligaments span the joint and should provide the restraint needed for the supported-joint goal.
expectation: The ligaments will reinforce the enclosed elbow while allowing movement.

effect: The ligaments completed the supported, movable elbow and the chapter's final goal.
reaction: The contrast between bending and resistance to sideways movement makes the ligaments' role clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Mineralising the collagen framework was most worthwhile: the planned inset and explanation connect collagen's toughness with mineral's resistance to compression.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding bone cells to the framework felt comparatively repetitive after their roles had already been described, although the channels were useful to picture.

surprise.text: The distinction between matrix-producing osteoblasts and osteocytes embedded in bone clarified that bone remains living tissue.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary; the supplied descriptions connected each component to the construction.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue to see how the assembled skeleton connects to muscle and movement; the joint construction made those relationships interesting.
